docs.title: hgetex()
docs.text:
hgetex(key, fields, options?): T

Gets hash fields and optionally sets their expiration.

docs.title: fields
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The fields in the hash stored at key to retrieve from the database.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
HGetExOptions

Optional arguments for the HGETEX command. See HGetExOptions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// Get fields without setting expiration
batch.hgetex("myHash", ["field1", "field2"]);

// Get fields and set 30 second expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 30 } }
);

// Get fields and remove expiration (make persistent)
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: "PERSIST" }
);

// Get fields and set millisecond precision expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field3"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Milliseconds, count: 5000 } }
);

Command Response - An array of values associated with the given fields, in the same order as they are requested. For every field that does not exist in the hash, a null value is returned. If key does not exist, returns an array of null values.

The number of field names to return. If count is positive, returns unique elements. If negative, allows for duplicates.

Command Response - A 2D array of [fieldName, value] arrays, where fieldName is a random field name from the hash and value is the associated value of the field name. If the hash does not exist or is empty, the response will be an empty array.

docs.title: cursor
docs.text:
string

The cursor that points to the next iteration of results. A value of "0" indicates the start of the search.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
HScanOptions

(Optional) The HScanOptions.

Command Response - An array of the cursor and the subset of the hash held by key. The first element is always the cursor for the next iteration of results. "0" will be the cursor returned on the last iteration of the hash. The second element is always an array of the subset of the hash held in key. The array in the second element is a flattened series of string pairs, where the value is at even indices and the value is at odd indices. If options.noValues is set to true, the second element will only contain the fields without the values.

docs.title: hsetex()
docs.text:
hsetex(key, fieldsAndValues, options?): T

Sets hash fields with expiration times and optional conditional changes.

docs.title: fieldsAndValues
docs.text:
A map or array of field-value pairs to set.

Record\<string, GlideString> | HashDataType

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
HSetExOptions

Optional parameters including field conditional changes and expiry settings. See HSetExOptions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// Set fields with 60 second expiration, only if none exist
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field1: "value1", field2: "value2" },
    {
        fieldConditionalChange: HashFieldConditionalChange.ONLY_IF_NONE_EXIST,
        expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 60 }
    }
);

// Set fields and keep existing TTL
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field3: "value3" },
    { expiry: "KEEPTTL" }
);

// Set fields with Unix timestamp expiration
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field4: "value4" },
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.UnixSeconds, count: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600 } }
);

Command Response - The number of fields that were added to the hash.

docs.title: lcsIdx()

Returns the indices and lengths of the longest common subsequences between strings stored at key1 and key2.

docs.title: key2
docs.text:

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) withMatchLen: if true, include the length of the substring matched for the each match. - (Optional) minMatchLen: the minimum length of matches to include in the result.

Command Response - A GlideRecord containing the indices of the longest common subsequences between the 2 strings and the lengths of the longest common subsequences. The resulting map contains two keys, "matches" and "len": - "len" is mapped to the total length of the all longest common subsequences between the 2 strings stored as an integer. This value doesn't count towards the minMatchLen filter. - "matches" is mapped to a three dimensional array of integers that stores pairs of indices that represent the location of the common subsequences in the strings held by key1 and key2.

Pops one or more elements from the first non-empty list from the provided keys.

docs.title: direction
docs.text:
ListDirection

The direction based on which elements are popped from - see ListDirection.

docs.title: count?
docs.text:
number

(Optional) The maximum number of popped elements.

Command Response - A Record which stores the key name where elements were popped out and the array of popped elements. If no member could be popped, returns null.

docs.title: lolwut()
docs.text:
lolwut(options?): T

Displays a piece of generative computer art and the server version.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
LolwutOptions

(Optional) The LOLWUT options - see LolwutOptions.

Command Response - A piece of generative computer art along with the current server version.

docs.title: lpop()
docs.text:
lpop(key): T

Removes and returns the first elements of the list stored at key. The command pops a single element from the beginning of the list.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list.

Command Response - The value of the first element. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: lpopCount()
docs.text:
lpopCount(key, count): T

Removes and returns up to count elements of the list stored at key, depending on the list's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the list.

Command Response - A list of the popped elements will be returned depending on the list's length. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: lpos()
docs.text:
lpos(key, element, options?): T

Returns the index of the first occurrence of element inside the list specified by key. If no match is found, null is returned. If the count option is specified, then the function returns an array of indices of matching elements within the list.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The value to search for within the list.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
LPosOptions

(Optional) The LPOS options - see LPosOptions.

Command Response - The index of element, or null if element is not in the list. If the count option is specified, then the function returns an array of indices of matching elements within the list.

docs.title: lpush()
docs.text:
lpush(key, elements): T

Inserts all the specified values at the head of the list stored at key. elements are inserted one after the other to the head of the list, from the leftmost element to the rightmost element. If key does not exist, it is created as empty list before performing the push operations.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the head of the list stored at key.

Command Response - the length of the list after the push operations.

docs.title: lpushx()
docs.text:
lpushx(key, elements): T

Inserts specified values at the head of the list, only if key already exists and holds a list.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the head of the list stored at key.

Command Response - The length of the list after the push operation.

docs.title: lrange()
docs.text:
lrange(key, start, end): T

Returns the specified elements of the list stored at key. The offsets start and end are zero-based indexes, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element and so on. These offsets can also be negative numbers indicating offsets starting at the end of the list, with -1 being the last element of the list, -2 being the penultimate, and so on.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
number

The end of the range.

Command Response - list of elements in the specified range. If start exceeds the end of the list, or if start is greater than end, an empty list will be returned. If end exceeds the actual end of the list, the range will stop at the actual end of the list. If key does not exist an empty list will be returned.

docs.title: lrem()
docs.text:
lrem(key, count, element): T

Removes the first count occurrences of elements equal to element from the list stored at key.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the occurrences of elements equal to element to remove. If count is positive : Removes elements equal to element moving from head to tail. If count is negative : Removes elements equal to element moving from tail to head. If count is 0 or count is greater than the occurrences of elements equal to element: Removes all elements equal to element.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The element to remove from the list.

Command Response - the number of the removed elements. If key does not exist, 0 is returned.

docs.title: lset()
docs.text:
lset(key, index, element): T

Sets the list element at index to element. The index is zero-based, so 0 means the first element, 1 the second element and so on. Negative indices can be used to designate elements starting at the tail of the list. Here, -1 means the last element, -2 means the penultimate and so forth.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
number

The index of the element in the list to be set.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The new element to set at the specified index.

Command Response - Always "OK".

docs.title: ltrim()
docs.text:
ltrim(key, start, end): T

Trim an existing list so that it will contain only the specified range of elements specified. The offsets start and end are zero-based indexes, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element and so on. These offsets can also be negative numbers indicating offsets starting at the end of the list, with -1 being the last element of the list, -2 being the penultimate, and so on.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
number

The end of the range.

Command Response - always "OK". If start exceeds the end of the list, or if start is greater than end, the list is emptied and the key is removed. If end exceeds the actual end of the list, it will be treated like the last element of the list. If key does not exist the command will be ignored.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of keys to retrieve values for.

Command Response - A list of values corresponding to the provided keys. If a key is not found, its corresponding value in the list will be null.

docs.title: move()
docs.text:
move(key, dbIndex): T

Move key from the currently selected database to the database specified by dbIndex.

docs.title: dbIndex
docs.text:
number

The index of the database to move key to.

Command Response - true if key was moved, or false if the key already exists in the destination database or does not exist in the source database.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: Move is available for cluster mode since Valkey 9.0.0 and above.

docs.title: mset()
docs.text:
mset(keysAndValues): T

Set multiple keys to multiple values in a single atomic operation.

docs.title: keysAndValues
docs.text:
A list of key-value pairs to set.

Command Response - always "OK".

Record\<string, GlideString> | GlideRecord\<GlideString>

docs.title: msetnx()
docs.text:
msetnx(keysAndValues): T

Sets multiple keys to values if the key does not exist. The operation is atomic, and if one or more keys already exist, the entire operation fails.

docs.title: keysAndValues
docs.text:
A list of key-value pairs to set. Command Response - true if all keys were set. false if no key was set.

Record\<string, GlideString> | GlideRecord\<GlideString>

docs.title: objectEncoding()
docs.text:
objectEncoding(key): T

Returns the internal encoding for the Valkey object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the internal encoding of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the internal encoding of the object stored at key as a string. Otherwise, returns None.

docs.title: objectFreq()
docs.text:
objectFreq(key): T

Returns the logarithmic access frequency counter of a Valkey object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the logarithmic access frequency counter of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the logarithmic access frequency counter of the object stored at key as a number. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: objectIdletime()
docs.text:
objectIdletime(key): T

Returns the time in seconds since the last access to the value stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the idle time of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the idle time in seconds. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: objectRefcount()
docs.text:
objectRefcount(key): T

Returns the reference count of the object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the reference count of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the reference count of the object stored at key as a number. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: persist()
docs.text:
persist(key): T

Removes the existing timeout on key, turning the key from volatile (a key with an expire set) to persistent (a key that will never expire as no timeout is associated).

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to remove the existing timeout on.

Command Response - false if key does not exist or does not have an associated timeout, true if the timeout has been removed.

docs.title: pexpire()
docs.text:
pexpire(key, milliseconds, options?): T

Sets a timeout on key in milliseconds. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. If milliseconds is non-positive number, the key will be deleted rather than expired. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to set timeout on it.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) expireOption: the expire option - see ExpireOptions.

Command Response - true if the timeout was set. false if the timeout was not set. e.g. key doesn't exist, or operation skipped due to the provided arguments.

docs.title: pexpireAt()
docs.text:
pexpireAt(key, unixMilliseconds, options?): T

Sets a timeout on key. It takes an absolute Unix timestamp (milliseconds since January 1, 1970) instead of specifying the number of milliseconds. A timestamp in the past will delete the key immediately. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to set timeout on it.

docs.title: unixMilliseconds
docs.text:
number

The timeout in an absolute Unix timestamp.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) expireOption: the expire option - see ExpireOptions.

Command Response - true if the timeout was set. false if the timeout was not set. e.g. key doesn't exist, or operation skipped due to the provided arguments.

docs.title: pexpireTime()
docs.text:
pexpireTime(key): T

Returns the absolute Unix timestamp (since January 1, 1970) at which the given key will expire, in milliseconds.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to determine the expiration value of.

Command Response - The expiration Unix timestamp in seconds, -2 if key does not exist or -1 if key exists but has no associated expire.

docs.title: pfadd()
docs.text:
pfadd(key, elements): T

Adds all elements to the HyperLogLog data structure stored at the specified key. Creates a new structure if the key does not exist. When no elements are provided, and key exists and is a HyperLogLog, then no operation is performed.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the HyperLogLog data structure to add elements into.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

An array of members to add to the HyperLogLog stored at key. Command Response - If the HyperLogLog is newly created, or if the HyperLogLog approximated cardinality is altered, then returns true. Otherwise, returns false.

docs.title: pfcount()
docs.text:
pfcount(keys): T

Estimates the cardinality of the data stored in a HyperLogLog structure for a single key or calculates the combined cardinality of multiple keys by merging their HyperLogLogs temporarily.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the HyperLogLog data structures to be analyzed. Command Response - The approximated cardinality of given HyperLogLog data structures. The cardinality of a key that does not exist is 0.

docs.title: pfmerge()
docs.text:
pfmerge(destination, sourceKeys): T

Merges multiple HyperLogLog values into a unique value. If the destination variable exists, it is treated as one of the source HyperLogLog data sets, otherwise a new HyperLogLog is created.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the destination HyperLogLog where the merged data sets will be stored.

docs.title: sourceKeys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the HyperLogLog structures to be merged. Command Response - A simple "OK" response.

docs.title: message?
docs.text:
GlideString

(Optional) A message to include in the PING command. - If not provided, the server will respond with "PONG". - If provided, the server will respond with a copy of the message.

Command Response - "PONG" if message is not provided, otherwise return a copy of message.

docs.title: pttl()
docs.text:
pttl(key): T

Returns the remaining time to live of key that has a timeout, in milliseconds.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return its timeout.

Command Response - TTL in milliseconds, -2 if key does not exist, -1 if key exists but has no associated expire.

docs.title: pubsubChannels()
docs.text:
pubsubChannels(pattern?): T

Lists the currently active channels. The command is routed to all nodes, and aggregates the response to a single array.

docs.title: pattern?
docs.text:
GlideString

A glob-style pattern to match active channels. If not provided, all active channels are returned. Command Response - A list of currently active channels matching the given pattern. If no pattern is specified, all active channels are returned.

docs.title: pubsubNumPat()
docs.text:
pubsubNumPat(): T

Returns the number of unique patterns that are subscribed to by clients.

Note: This is the total number of unique patterns all the clients are subscribed to, not the count of clients subscribed to patterns. The command is routed to all nodes, and aggregates the response to the sum of all pattern subscriptions.

docs.title: See
docs.text:
valkey.io for more details.

Command Response - The number of unique patterns.

docs.title: pubsubNumSub()
docs.text:
pubsubNumSub(channels): T

Returns the number of subscribers (exclusive of clients subscribed to patterns) for the specified channels.

docs.title: channels
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The list of channels to query for the number of subscribers.

Command Response - A list of the channel names and their numbers of subscribers.

docs.title: randomKey()
docs.text:
randomKey(): T

Returns a random existing key name from the currently selected database.

docs.title: See
docs.text:
valkey.io for details.

Command Response - A random existing key name from the currently selected database.

docs.title: rename()
docs.text:
rename(key, newKey): T

Renames key to newkey. If newkey already exists it is overwritten.

docs.title: newKey
docs.text:
GlideString

The new name of the key.

Command Response - If the key was successfully renamed, return "OK". If key does not exist, an error is thrown.

docs.title: renamenx()
docs.text:
renamenx(key, newKey): T

Renames key to newkey if newkey does not yet exist.

docs.title: newKey
docs.text:
GlideString

The new name of the key.

Command Response - If the key was successfully renamed, returns true. Otherwise, returns false. If key does not exist, an error is thrown.

docs.title: restore()
docs.text:
restore(key, ttl, value, options?): T

Create a key associated with a value that is obtained by deserializing the provided serialized value (obtained via dump).

docs.title: ttl
docs.text:
number

The expiry time (in milliseconds). If 0, the key will persist.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
Buffer

The serialized value to deserialize and assign to key.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
RestoreOptions

(Optional) Restore options RestoreOptions.

Command Response - Return "OK" if the key was successfully restored with a value.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: options.idletime and options.frequency modifiers cannot be set at the same time.

docs.title: rpop()
docs.text:
rpop(key): T

Removes and returns the last elements of the list stored at key. The command pops a single element from the end of the list.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list.

Command Response - The value of the last element. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: rpopCount()
docs.text:
rpopCount(key, count): T

Removes and returns up to count elements from the list stored at key, depending on the list's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the list.

Command Response - A list of popped elements will be returned depending on the list's length. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: rpush()
docs.text:
rpush(key, elements): T

Inserts all the specified values at the tail of the list stored at key. elements are inserted one after the other to the tail of the list, from the leftmost element to the rightmost element. If key does not exist, it is created as empty list before performing the push operations.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the tail of the list stored at key.

Command Response - the length of the list after the push operations.

docs.title: rpushx()
docs.text:
rpushx(key, elements): T

Inserts specified values at the tail of the list, only if key already exists and holds a list.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the tail of the list stored at key.

Command Response - The length of the list after the push operation.

docs.title: sadd()
docs.text:
sadd(key, members): T

Adds the specified members to the set stored at key. Specified members that are already a member of this set are ignored. If key does not exist, a new set is created before adding members.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to store the members to its set.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of members to add to the set stored at key.

Command Response - the number of members that were added to the set, not including all the members already present in the set.

docs.title: scard()
docs.text:
scard(key): T

Returns the set cardinality (number of elements) of the set stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return the number of its members.

Command Response - the cardinality (number of elements) of the set, or 0 if key does not exist.

docs.title: sdiff()
docs.text:
sdiff(keys): T

Computes the difference between the first set and all the successive sets in keys.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to diff.

Command Response - A Set of elements representing the difference between the sets. If a key in keys does not exist, it is treated as an empty set.

docs.title: sdiffstore()
docs.text:
sdiffstore(destination, keys): T

Stores the difference between the first set and all the successive sets in keys into a new set at destination.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to diff.

Command Response - The number of elements in the resulting set.

docs.title: set()
docs.text:
set(key, value, options?): T

Set the given key with the given value. Return value is dependent on the passed options.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
GlideString

The value to store with the given key.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SetOptions

The set options.

Command Response - If the value is successfully set, return OK. If value isn't set because of onlyIfExists or onlyIfDoesNotExist conditions, return null. If returnOldValue is set, return the old value as a string.

docs.title: setbit()
docs.text:
setbit(key, offset, value): T

Sets or clears the bit at offset in the string value stored at key. The offset is a zero-based index, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element, and so on. The offset must be less than 2^32 and greater than or equal to 0. If a key is non-existent then the bit at offset is set to value and the preceding bits are set to 0.

docs.title: offset
docs.text:
number

The index of the bit to be set.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
number

The bit value to set at offset. The value must be 0 or 1.

Command Response - The bit value that was previously stored at offset.

docs.title: setrange()
docs.text:
setrange(key, offset, value): T

Overwrites part of the string stored at key, starting at the specified byte offset, for the entire length of value. If the offset is larger than the current length of the string at key, the string is padded with zero bytes to make offset fit. Creates the key if it doesn't exist.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the string to update.

docs.title: offset
docs.text:
number

The byte position in the string where value should be written.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
GlideString

The string written with offset.

Command Response - The length of the string stored at key after it was modified.

docs.title: sinter()
docs.text:
sinter(keys): T

Gets the intersection of all the given sets. When in cluster mode, all keys must map to the same hash slot.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to get the intersection.

Command Response - A set of members which are present in all given sets. If one or more sets do not exist, an empty set will be returned.

docs.title: sintercard()
docs.text:
sintercard(keys, options?): T

Gets the cardinality of the intersection of all the given sets.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) limit: the limit for the intersection cardinality value. If not specified, or set to 0, no limit is used.

Command Response - The cardinality of the intersection result. If one or more sets do not exist, 0 is returned.

docs.title: sinterstore()
docs.text:
sinterstore(destination, keys): T

Stores the members of the intersection of all given sets specified by keys into a new set at destination.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys from which to retrieve the set members.

Command Response - The number of elements in the resulting set.

docs.title: sismember()
docs.text:
sismember(key, member): T

Returns if member is a member of the set stored at key.

docs.title: member
docs.text:
GlideString

The member to check for existence in the set.

Command Response - true if the member exists in the set, false otherwise. If key doesn't exist, it is treated as an empty set and the command returns false.

docs.title: smembers()
docs.text:
smembers(key): T

Returns all the members of the set value stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return its members.

Command Response - all members of the set. If key does not exist, it is treated as an empty set and this command returns empty list.

docs.title: smismember()
docs.text:
smismember(key, members): T

Checks whether each member is contained in the members of the set stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to check.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of members to check for existence in the set.

Command Response - An array of boolean values, each indicating if the respective member exists in the set.

docs.title: smove()
docs.text:
smove(source, destination, member): T

Moves member from the set at source to the set at destination, removing it from the source set. Creates a new destination set if needed. The operation is atomic.

docs.title: source
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to remove the element from.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to add the element to.

docs.title: member
docs.text:
GlideString

The set element to move.

Command Response - true on success, or false if the source set does not exist or the element is not a member of the source set.

docs.title: sort()
docs.text:
sort(key, options?): T

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and returns the result.

The sort command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements.

To store the result into a new key, see sortStore.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - An Array of sorted elements.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: When in cluster mode, both key and the patterns specified in SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns must map to the same hash slot. The use of SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns in cluster mode is supported since Valkey version 8.0.

docs.title: sortReadOnly()
docs.text:
sortReadOnly(key, options?): T

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and returns the result.

The sortReadOnly command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements.

This command is routed depending on the client's ReadFrom strategy.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - An Array of sorted elements

docs.title: sortStore()
docs.text:
sortStore(key, destination, options?): T

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and stores the result in destination.

The sort command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements, and store the result in a new key.

To get the sort result without storing it into a key, see sort or sortReadOnly.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key where the sorted result will be stored.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - The number of elements in the sorted key stored at destination.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: When in cluster mode, key, destination and the patterns specified in SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns must map to the same hash slot. The use of SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns in cluster mode is supported since Valkey version 8.0.

docs.title: spop()
docs.text:
spop(key): T

Removes and returns one random member from the set value store at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set.

Command Response - the value of the popped member. If key does not exist, null will be returned.

docs.title: See
docs.text: valkey.io for details. To pop multiple members, see spopCount.

docs.title: spopCount()
docs.text:
spopCount(key, count): T

Removes and returns up to count random members from the set value store at key, depending on the set's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the set.

Command Response - A list of popped elements will be returned depending on the set's length. If key does not exist, empty list will be returned.

docs.title: srandmember()
docs.text:
srandmember(key): T

Returns a random element from the set value stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key from which to retrieve the set member. Command Response - A random element from the set, or null if key does not exist.

docs.title: srandmemberCount()
docs.text:
srandmemberCount(key, count): T

Returns one or more random elements from the set value stored at key.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The number of members to return. If count is positive, returns unique members. If count is negative, allows for duplicates members. Command Response - A list of members from the set. If the set does not exist or is empty, an empty list will be returned.

docs.title: srem()
docs.text:
srem(key, members): T

Removes the specified members from the set stored at key. Specified members that are not a member of this set are ignored.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to remove the members from its set.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of members to remove from the set stored at key.

Command Response - the number of members that were removed from the set, not including non existing members. If key does not exist, it is treated as an empty set and this command returns 0.

docs.title: Class: Batch
docs.text: Batch implementation for standalone GlideClient. Batches allow the execution of a group of commands in a single step.

docs.title: Batch Response:
docs.text: An array of command responses is returned by the client exec command, in the order they were given. Each element in the array represents a command given to the batch. The response for each command depends on the executed Valkey command. Specific response types are documented alongside each method.

docs.title: Param
docs.text: Indicates whether the batch is atomic or non-atomic. If true, the batch will be executed as an atomic transaction. If false, the batch will be executed as a non-atomic pipeline.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: Standalone Batches are executed on the primary node.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
// Example of Atomic Batch (Transaction)
const transaction = new Batch(true) // Atomic (Transactional)
    .set("key", "value")
    .get("key");
const result = await client.exec(transaction, true);
// result contains: OK and "value"
console.log(result); // ["OK", "value"]

// Example of Non-Atomic Batch (Pipeline)
const pipeline = new Batch(false) // Non-Atomic (Pipeline)
    .set("key1", "value1")
    .set("key2", "value2")
    .get("key1")
    .get("key2");
const result = await client.exec(pipeline, true);
// result contains: OK, OK, "value1", "value2"
console.log(result); // ["OK", "OK", "value1", "value2"]

docs.title: geosearch()

docs.title: searchFrom
docs.text:
SearchOrigin

The query's center point options, could be one of:

  • MemberOrigin to use the position of the given existing member in the sorted set.

  • CoordOrigin to use the given longitude and latitude coordinates.

docs.title: searchBy
docs.text:
GeoSearchShape

The query's shape options, could be one of:

  • GeoCircleShape to search inside circular area according to given radius.

  • GeoBoxShape to search inside an axis-aligned rectangle, determined by height and width.

docs.title: resultOptions?
docs.text:
GeoSearchResultOptions

The optional inputs to request additional information and configure sorting/limiting the results, see GeoSearchResultOptions.

Command Response - By default, returns an Array of members (locations) names. If any of withCoord, withDist or withHash are set to true in GeoSearchResultOptions, a 2D Array returned, where each sub-array represents a single item in the following order:

  • The distance from the center as a floating point number, in the same unit specified for searchBy.
  • The geohash of the location as a integer number.
  • The coordinates as a two item array of floating point numbers.

docs.title: hgetex()
docs.text:
hgetex(key, fields, options?): Batch

Gets hash fields and optionally sets their expiration.

docs.title: fields
docs.text:

The fields in the hash stored at key to retrieve from the database.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
HGetExOptions

Optional arguments for the HGETEX command. See HGetExOptions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// Get fields without setting expiration
batch.hgetex("myHash", ["field1", "field2"]);

// Get fields and set 30 second expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 30 } }
);

// Get fields and remove expiration (make persistent)
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: "PERSIST" }
);

// Get fields and set millisecond precision expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field3"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Milliseconds, count: 5000 } }
);

Command Response - An array of values associated with the given fields, in the same order as they are requested. For every field that does not exist in the hash, a null value is returned. If key does not exist, returns an array of null values.

docs.text:
// Set fields with 60 second expiration, only if none exist
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field1: "value1", field2: "value2" },
    {
        fieldConditionalChange: HashFieldConditionalChange.ONLY_IF_NONE_EXIST,
        expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 60 }

);

// Set fields and keep existing TTL
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field3: "value3" },
    { expiry: "KEEPTTL" }
);

// Set fields with Unix timestamp expiration
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field4: "value4" },
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.UnixSeconds, count: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600 } }
);

ListDirection

The ListDirection to remove the element from.

docs.title: whereTo
docs.text:
ListDirection

The ListDirection to add the element to.

Command Response - The popped element, or null if source does not exist.

docs.title: lmpop()
docs.text:
lmpop(keys, direction, count?): Batch

Pops one or more elements from the first non-empty list from the provided keys.

docs.title: direction
docs.text:
ListDirection

The direction based on which elements are popped from - see ListDirection.

docs.title: count?
docs.text:
number

(Optional) The maximum number of popped elements.

Command Response - A Record which stores the key name where elements were popped out and the array of popped elements. If no member could be popped, returns null.

docs.title: lolwut()
docs.text:
lolwut(options?): Batch

Displays a piece of generative computer art and the server version.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
LolwutOptions

(Optional) The LOLWUT options - see LolwutOptions.

Command Response - A piece of generative computer art along with the current server version.

docs.title: lpop()
docs.text:
lpop(key): Batch

Removes and returns the first elements of the list stored at key. The command pops a single element from the beginning of the list.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list.

Command Response - The value of the first element. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: lpopCount()
docs.text:
lpopCount(key, count): Batch

Removes and returns up to count elements of the list stored at key, depending on the list's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the list.

Command Response - A list of the popped elements will be returned depending on the list's length. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: lpos()
docs.text:
lpos(key, element, options?): Batch

Returns the index of the first occurrence of element inside the list specified by key. If no match is found, null is returned. If the count option is specified, then the function returns an array of indices of matching elements within the list.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The value to search for within the list.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
LPosOptions

(Optional) The LPOS options - see LPosOptions.

Command Response - The index of element, or null if element is not in the list. If the count option is specified, then the function returns an array of indices of matching elements within the list.

docs.title: lpush()
docs.text:
lpush(key, elements): Batch

Inserts all the specified values at the head of the list stored at key. elements are inserted one after the other to the head of the list, from the leftmost element to the rightmost element. If key does not exist, it is created as empty list before performing the push operations.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the head of the list stored at key.

Command Response - the length of the list after the push operations.

docs.title: lpushx()
docs.text:
lpushx(key, elements): Batch

Inserts specified values at the head of the list, only if key already exists and holds a list.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the head of the list stored at key.

Command Response - The length of the list after the push operation.

docs.title: lrange()
docs.text:
lrange(key, start, end): Batch

Returns the specified elements of the list stored at key. The offsets start and end are zero-based indexes, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element and so on. These offsets can also be negative numbers indicating offsets starting at the end of the list, with -1 being the last element of the list, -2 being the penultimate, and so on.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
number

The end of the range.

Command Response - list of elements in the specified range. If start exceeds the end of the list, or if start is greater than end, an empty list will be returned. If end exceeds the actual end of the list, the range will stop at the actual end of the list. If key does not exist an empty list will be returned.

docs.title: lrem()
docs.text:
lrem(key, count, element): Batch

Removes the first count occurrences of elements equal to element from the list stored at key.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the occurrences of elements equal to element to remove. If count is positive : Removes elements equal to element moving from head to tail. If count is negative : Removes elements equal to element moving from tail to head. If count is 0 or count is greater than the occurrences of elements equal to element: Removes all elements equal to element.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The element to remove from the list.

Command Response - the number of the removed elements. If key does not exist, 0 is returned.

docs.title: lset()
docs.text:
lset(key, index, element): Batch

Sets the list element at index to element. The index is zero-based, so 0 means the first element, 1 the second element and so on. Negative indices can be used to designate elements starting at the tail of the list. Here, -1 means the last element, -2 means the penultimate and so forth.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
number

The index of the element in the list to be set.

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GlideString

The new element to set at the specified index.

Command Response - Always "OK".

docs.title: ltrim()
docs.text:
ltrim(key, start, end): Batch

Trim an existing list so that it will contain only the specified range of elements specified. The offsets start and end are zero-based indexes, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element and so on. These offsets can also be negative numbers indicating offsets starting at the end of the list, with -1 being the last element of the list, -2 being the penultimate, and so on.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
number

The end of the range.

Command Response - always "OK". If start exceeds the end of the list, or if start is greater than end, the list is emptied and the key is removed. If end exceeds the actual end of the list, it will be treated like the last element of the list. If key does not exist the command will be ignored.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of keys to retrieve values for.

Command Response - A list of values corresponding to the provided keys. If a key is not found, its corresponding value in the list will be null.

docs.title: move()
docs.text:
move(key, dbIndex): Batch

Move key from the currently selected database to the database specified by dbIndex.

docs.title: dbIndex
docs.text:
number

The index of the database to move key to.

Command Response - true if key was moved, or false if the key already exists in the destination database or does not exist in the source database.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: Move is available for cluster mode since Valkey 9.0.0 and above.

docs.title: mset()
docs.text:
mset(keysAndValues): Batch

Set multiple keys to multiple values in a single atomic operation.

docs.title: keysAndValues
docs.text:
A list of key-value pairs to set.

Command Response - always "OK".

Record\<string, GlideString> | GlideRecord\<GlideString>

docs.title: msetnx()
docs.text:
msetnx(keysAndValues): Batch

Sets multiple keys to values if the key does not exist. The operation is atomic, and if one or more keys already exist, the entire operation fails.

docs.title: keysAndValues
docs.text:
A list of key-value pairs to set. Command Response - true if all keys were set. false if no key was set.

Record\<string, GlideString> | GlideRecord\<GlideString>

docs.title: objectEncoding()
docs.text:
objectEncoding(key): Batch

Returns the internal encoding for the Valkey object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the internal encoding of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the internal encoding of the object stored at key as a string. Otherwise, returns None.

docs.title: objectFreq()
docs.text:
objectFreq(key): Batch

Returns the logarithmic access frequency counter of a Valkey object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the logarithmic access frequency counter of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the logarithmic access frequency counter of the object stored at key as a number. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: objectIdletime()
docs.text:
objectIdletime(key): Batch

Returns the time in seconds since the last access to the value stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the idle time of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the idle time in seconds. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: objectRefcount()
docs.text:
objectRefcount(key): Batch

Returns the reference count of the object stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the object to get the reference count of.

Command Response - If key exists, returns the reference count of the object stored at key as a number. Otherwise, returns null.

docs.title: persist()
docs.text:
persist(key): Batch

Removes the existing timeout on key, turning the key from volatile (a key with an expire set) to persistent (a key that will never expire as no timeout is associated).

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to remove the existing timeout on.

Command Response - false if key does not exist or does not have an associated timeout, true if the timeout has been removed.

docs.title: pexpire()
docs.text:
pexpire(key, milliseconds, options?): Batch

Sets a timeout on key in milliseconds. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. If milliseconds is non-positive number, the key will be deleted rather than expired. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to set timeout on it.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) expireOption: the expire option - see ExpireOptions.

Command Response - true if the timeout was set. false if the timeout was not set. e.g. key doesn't exist, or operation skipped due to the provided arguments.

docs.title: pexpireAt()
docs.text:
pexpireAt(key, unixMilliseconds, options?): Batch

Sets a timeout on key. It takes an absolute Unix timestamp (milliseconds since January 1, 1970) instead of specifying the number of milliseconds. A timestamp in the past will delete the key immediately. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to set timeout on it.

docs.title: unixMilliseconds
docs.text:
number

The timeout in an absolute Unix timestamp.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) expireOption: the expire option - see ExpireOptions.

Command Response - true if the timeout was set. false if the timeout was not set. e.g. key doesn't exist, or operation skipped due to the provided arguments.

docs.title: pexpireTime()
docs.text:
pexpireTime(key): Batch

Returns the absolute Unix timestamp (since January 1, 1970) at which the given key will expire, in milliseconds.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to determine the expiration value of.

Command Response - The expiration Unix timestamp in seconds, -2 if key does not exist or -1 if key exists but has no associated expire.

docs.title: pfadd()
docs.text:
pfadd(key, elements): Batch

Adds all elements to the HyperLogLog data structure stored at the specified key. Creates a new structure if the key does not exist. When no elements are provided, and key exists and is a HyperLogLog, then no operation is performed.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the HyperLogLog data structure to add elements into.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

An array of members to add to the HyperLogLog stored at key. Command Response - If the HyperLogLog is newly created, or if the HyperLogLog approximated cardinality is altered, then returns true. Otherwise, returns false.

docs.title: pfcount()
docs.text:
pfcount(keys): Batch

Estimates the cardinality of the data stored in a HyperLogLog structure for a single key or calculates the combined cardinality of multiple keys by merging their HyperLogLogs temporarily.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the HyperLogLog data structures to be analyzed. Command Response - The approximated cardinality of given HyperLogLog data structures. The cardinality of a key that does not exist is 0.

docs.title: pfmerge()
docs.text:
pfmerge(destination, sourceKeys): Batch

Merges multiple HyperLogLog values into a unique value. If the destination variable exists, it is treated as one of the source HyperLogLog data sets, otherwise a new HyperLogLog is created.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the destination HyperLogLog where the merged data sets will be stored.

docs.title: sourceKeys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the HyperLogLog structures to be merged. Command Response - A simple "OK" response.

docs.title: message?
docs.text:
GlideString

(Optional) A message to include in the PING command. - If not provided, the server will respond with "PONG". - If provided, the server will respond with a copy of the message.

Command Response - "PONG" if message is not provided, otherwise return a copy of message.

docs.title: pttl()
docs.text:
pttl(key): Batch

Returns the remaining time to live of key that has a timeout, in milliseconds.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return its timeout.

Command Response - TTL in milliseconds, -2 if key does not exist, -1 if key exists but has no associated expire.

docs.title: channel
docs.text:
GlideString

Channel to publish the message on.

Command Response - Number of subscriptions in primary node that received the message. Note that this value does not include subscriptions that configured on replicas.

docs.title: pubsubChannels()
docs.text:
pubsubChannels(pattern?): Batch

Lists the currently active channels. The command is routed to all nodes, and aggregates the response to a single array.

docs.title: pattern?
docs.text:
GlideString

A glob-style pattern to match active channels. If not provided, all active channels are returned. Command Response - A list of currently active channels matching the given pattern. If no pattern is specified, all active channels are returned.

docs.title: pubsubNumPat()
docs.text:
pubsubNumPat(): Batch

Returns the number of unique patterns that are subscribed to by clients.

Note: This is the total number of unique patterns all the clients are subscribed to, not the count of clients subscribed to patterns. The command is routed to all nodes, and aggregates the response to the sum of all pattern subscriptions.

docs.title: See
docs.text:
valkey.io for more details.

Command Response - The number of unique patterns.

docs.title: pubsubNumSub()
docs.text:
pubsubNumSub(channels): Batch

Returns the number of subscribers (exclusive of clients subscribed to patterns) for the specified channels.

docs.title: channels
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The list of channels to query for the number of subscribers.

Command Response - A list of the channel names and their numbers of subscribers.

docs.title: randomKey()
docs.text:
randomKey(): Batch

Returns a random existing key name from the currently selected database.

docs.title: See
docs.text:
valkey.io for details.

Command Response - A random existing key name from the currently selected database.

docs.title: rename()
docs.text:
rename(key, newKey): Batch

Renames key to newkey. If newkey already exists it is overwritten.

docs.title: newKey
docs.text:
GlideString

The new name of the key.

Command Response - If the key was successfully renamed, return "OK". If key does not exist, an error is thrown.

docs.title: renamenx()
docs.text:
renamenx(key, newKey): Batch

Renames key to newkey if newkey does not yet exist.

docs.title: newKey
docs.text:
GlideString

The new name of the key.

Command Response - If the key was successfully renamed, returns true. Otherwise, returns false. If key does not exist, an error is thrown.

docs.title: restore()
docs.text:
restore(key, ttl, value, options?): Batch

Create a key associated with a value that is obtained by deserializing the provided serialized value (obtained via dump).

docs.title: ttl
docs.text:
number

The expiry time (in milliseconds). If 0, the key will persist.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
Buffer

The serialized value to deserialize and assign to key.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
RestoreOptions

(Optional) Restore options RestoreOptions.

Command Response - Return "OK" if the key was successfully restored with a value.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: options.idletime and options.frequency modifiers cannot be set at the same time.

docs.title: rpop()
docs.text:
rpop(key): Batch

Removes and returns the last elements of the list stored at key. The command pops a single element from the end of the list.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list.

Command Response - The value of the last element. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: rpopCount()
docs.text:
rpopCount(key, count): Batch

Removes and returns up to count elements from the list stored at key, depending on the list's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the list.

Command Response - A list of popped elements will be returned depending on the list's length. If key does not exist null will be returned.

docs.title: rpush()
docs.text:
rpush(key, elements): Batch

Inserts all the specified values at the tail of the list stored at key. elements are inserted one after the other to the tail of the list, from the leftmost element to the rightmost element. If key does not exist, it is created as empty list before performing the push operations.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the tail of the list stored at key.

Command Response - the length of the list after the push operations.

docs.title: rpushx()
docs.text:
rpushx(key, elements): Batch

Inserts specified values at the tail of the list, only if key already exists and holds a list.

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The elements to insert at the tail of the list stored at key.

Command Response - The length of the list after the push operation.

docs.title: sadd()
docs.text:
sadd(key, members): Batch

Adds the specified members to the set stored at key. Specified members that are already a member of this set are ignored. If key does not exist, a new set is created before adding members.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to store the members to its set.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of members to add to the set stored at key.

Command Response - the number of members that were added to the set, not including all the members already present in the set.

docs.title: scard()
docs.text:
scard(key): Batch

Returns the set cardinality (number of elements) of the set stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return the number of its members.

Command Response - the cardinality (number of elements) of the set, or 0 if key does not exist.

docs.title: sdiff()
docs.text:
sdiff(keys): Batch

Computes the difference between the first set and all the successive sets in keys.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to diff.

Command Response - A Set of elements representing the difference between the sets. If a key in keys does not exist, it is treated as an empty set.

docs.title: sdiffstore()
docs.text:
sdiffstore(destination, keys): Batch

Stores the difference between the first set and all the successive sets in keys into a new set at destination.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to diff.

Command Response - The number of elements in the resulting set.

docs.title: select()
docs.text:
select(index): Batch

Change the currently selected database.

WARNING: This command is NOT RECOMMENDED for production use. Upon reconnection, the client will revert to the database_id specified in the client configuration (default: 0), NOT the database selected via this command.

RECOMMENDED APPROACH: Use the databaseId parameter in client configuration instead of using SELECT in batch operations.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
number

The index of the database to select.

Command Response - A simple "OK" response.

docs.title: set()
docs.text:
set(key, value, options?): Batch

Set the given key with the given value. Return value is dependent on the passed options.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
GlideString

The value to store with the given key.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SetOptions

The set options.

Command Response - If the value is successfully set, return OK. If value isn't set because of onlyIfExists or onlyIfDoesNotExist conditions, return null. If returnOldValue is set, return the old value as a string.

docs.title: setbit()
docs.text:
setbit(key, offset, value): Batch

Sets or clears the bit at offset in the string value stored at key. The offset is a zero-based index, with 0 being the first element of the list, 1 being the next element, and so on. The offset must be less than 2^32 and greater than or equal to 0. If a key is non-existent then the bit at offset is set to value and the preceding bits are set to 0.

docs.title: offset
docs.text:
number

The index of the bit to be set.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
number

The bit value to set at offset. The value must be 0 or 1.

Command Response - The bit value that was previously stored at offset.

docs.title: setrange()
docs.text:
setrange(key, offset, value): Batch

Overwrites part of the string stored at key, starting at the specified byte offset, for the entire length of value. If the offset is larger than the current length of the string at key, the string is padded with zero bytes to make offset fit. Creates the key if it doesn't exist.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the string to update.

docs.title: offset
docs.text:
number

The byte position in the string where value should be written.

docs.title: value
docs.text:
GlideString

The string written with offset.

Command Response - The length of the string stored at key after it was modified.

docs.title: sinter()
docs.text:
sinter(keys): Batch

Gets the intersection of all the given sets. When in cluster mode, all keys must map to the same hash slot.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys of the sets to get the intersection.

Command Response - A set of members which are present in all given sets. If one or more sets do not exist, an empty set will be returned.

docs.title: sintercard()
docs.text:
sintercard(keys, options?): Batch

Gets the cardinality of the intersection of all the given sets.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) limit: the limit for the intersection cardinality value. If not specified, or set to 0, no limit is used.

Command Response - The cardinality of the intersection result. If one or more sets do not exist, 0 is returned.

docs.title: sinterstore()
docs.text:
sinterstore(destination, keys): Batch

Stores the members of the intersection of all given sets specified by keys into a new set at destination.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
GlideString[]

The keys from which to retrieve the set members.

Command Response - The number of elements in the resulting set.

docs.title: sismember()
docs.text:
sismember(key, member): Batch

Returns if member is a member of the set stored at key.

docs.title: member
docs.text:
GlideString

The member to check for existence in the set.

Command Response - true if the member exists in the set, false otherwise. If key doesn't exist, it is treated as an empty set and the command returns false.

docs.title: smembers()
docs.text:
smembers(key): Batch

Returns all the members of the set value stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key to return its members.

Command Response - all members of the set. If key does not exist, it is treated as an empty set and this command returns empty list.

docs.title: smismember()
docs.text:
smismember(key, members): Batch

Checks whether each member is contained in the members of the set stored at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to check.

docs.title: members
docs.text:
GlideString[]

A list of members to check for existence in the set.

Command Response - An array of boolean values, each indicating if the respective member exists in the set.

docs.title: smove()
docs.text:
smove(source, destination, member): Batch

Moves member from the set at source to the set at destination, removing it from the source set. Creates a new destination set if needed. The operation is atomic.

docs.title: source
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to remove the element from.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set to add the element to.

docs.title: member
docs.text:
GlideString

The set element to move.

Command Response - true on success, or false if the source set does not exist or the element is not a member of the source set.

docs.title: sort()
docs.text:
sort(key, options?): Batch

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and returns the result.

The sort command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements.

To store the result into a new key, see sortStore.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - An Array of sorted elements.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: When in cluster mode, both key and the patterns specified in SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns must map to the same hash slot. The use of SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns in cluster mode is supported since Valkey version 8.0.

docs.title: sortReadOnly()
docs.text:
sortReadOnly(key, options?): Batch

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and returns the result.

The sortReadOnly command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements.

This command is routed depending on the client's ReadFrom strategy.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - An Array of sorted elements

docs.title: sortStore()
docs.text:
sortStore(key, destination, options?): Batch

Sorts the elements in the list, set, or sorted set at key and stores the result in destination.

The sort command can be used to sort elements based on different criteria and apply transformations on sorted elements, and store the result in a new key.

To get the sort result without storing it into a key, see sort or sortReadOnly.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the list, set, or sorted set to be sorted.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key where the sorted result will be stored.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
SortOptions

(Optional) SortOptions.

Command Response - The number of elements in the sorted key stored at destination.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: When in cluster mode, key, destination and the patterns specified in SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns must map to the same hash slot. The use of SortOptions.byPattern and SortOptions.getPatterns in cluster mode is supported since Valkey version 8.0.

docs.title: spop()
docs.text:
spop(key): Batch

Removes and returns one random member from the set value store at key.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the set.

Command Response - the value of the popped member. If key does not exist, null will be returned.

docs.title: See
docs.text: valkey.io for details. To pop multiple members, see spopCount.

docs.title: spopCount()
docs.text:
spopCount(key, count): Batch

Removes and returns up to count random members from the set value store at key, depending on the set's length.

docs.title: count
docs.text:
number

The count of the elements to pop from the set.

Command Response - A list of popped elements will be returned depending on the set's length. If key does not exist, empty list will be returned.

docs.title: srandmember()
docs.text:

These IDs are deleted from the Pending Entries List.

These IDs are deleted from the Pending Entries List.

docs.text:
The range query object representing the type of range query to perform. - For range queries by index (rank), use RangeByIndex. - For range queries by lexicographical order, use RangeByLex. - For range queries by score, use RangeByScore.

docs.text:
boolean = false

If true, reverses the sorted set, with index 0 as the element with the highest score.

Command Response - A list of elements within the specified range. If key does not exist, it is treated as an empty sorted set, and the command returns an empty array.

docs.title: rangeQuery
docs.text:
The range query object representing the type of range query to perform. - For range queries by index (rank), use RangeByIndex. - For range queries by lexicographical order, use RangeByLex. - For range queries by score, use RangeByScore.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.text:

Removes the specified members from the sorted set stored at key. Specified members that are not a member of this set are ignored.

docs.text:

docs.title: zremRangeByLex()
docs.text:
zremRangeByLex(key, minLex, maxLex): Batch

Removes all elements in the sorted set stored at key with lexicographical order between minLex and maxLex.

docs.title: minLex
docs.text:
Boundary\<GlideString>

The minimum lex to count from. Can be negative infinity, or a specific lex and inclusivity.

docs.title: maxLex

docs.title: zremRangeByRank()
docs.text:
zremRangeByRank(key, start, end): Batch

Removes all elements in the sorted set stored at key with rank between start and end. Both start and end are zero-based indexes with 0 being the element with the lowest score. These indexes can be negative numbers, where they indicate offsets starting at the element with the highest score.

docs.title: end
docs.text:
number

Command Response - The number of members removed. If start exceeds the end of the sorted set, or if start is greater than end, 0 returned. If end exceeds the actual end of the sorted set, the range will stop at the actual end of the sorted set. If key does not exist 0 will be returned.

docs.title: zremRangeByScore()

docs.title: cursor
docs.text:
string

The cursor that points to the next iteration of results. A value of "0" indicates the start of the search.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
ZScanOptions

(Optional) The zscan options - see ZScanOptions

Command Response - An Array of the cursor and the subset of the sorted set held by key. The first element is always the cursor for the next iteration of results. 0 will be the cursor returned on the last iteration of the sorted set. The second element is always an Array of the subset of the sorted set held in key. The Array in the second element is a flattened series of String pairs, where the value is at even indices and the score is at odd indices. If options.noScores is to true, the second element will only contain the members without scores.

docs.title: zunion()
docs.text:
zunion(keys): Batch

Computes the union of sorted sets given by the specified keys and returns a list of union elements.

To get the scores as well, see zunionWithScores. To store the result in a key as a sorted set, see zunionstore.

docs.title: zunionstore()
docs.text:
zunionstore(destination, keys, options?): Batch

Computes the union of sorted sets given by the specified keys and stores the result in destination. If destination already exists, it is overwritten. Otherwise, a new sorted set will be created. To get the result directly, see zunionWithScores.

docs.title: destination
docs.text:
GlideString

The key of the destination sorted set.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
The keys of the sorted sets with possible formats: - GlideString[] - for keys only. - KeyWeight[] - for weighted keys with their score multipliers.

GlideString[] | KeyWeight[]

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) aggregationType: the aggregation strategy to apply when combining the scores of elements. See AggregationType. If aggregationType is not specified, defaults to AggregationType.SUM.

Command Response - The number of elements in the resulting sorted set stored at destination.

docs.title: zunionWithScores()
docs.text:
zunionWithScores(keys, options?): Batch

Computes the intersection of sorted sets given by the specified keys and returns a list of union elements with scores. To get the elements only, see zunion.

docs.title: keys
docs.text:
The keys of the sorted sets with possible formats: - GlideString[] - for keys only. - KeyWeight[] - for weighted keys with their score multipliers.

GlideString[] | KeyWeight[]

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
(Optional) Additional parameters: - (Optional) aggregationType: the aggregation strategy to apply when combining the scores of elements. See AggregationType. If aggregationType is not specified, defaults to AggregationType.SUM.

Command Response - A list of elements and their scores representing the intersection of the sorted sets. The response comes in format GlideRecord<number>, see GlideRecord.

docs.title: Class: ClusterBatch
docs.text: Batch implementation for standalone GlideClusterClient. Batches allow the execution of a group of commands in a single step.

docs.title: Batch Response:
docs.text: An array of command responses is returned by the client exec command, in the order they were given. Each element in the array represents a command given to the batch. The response for each command depends on the executed Valkey command. Specific response types are documented alongside each method.

docs.title: Param
docs.text: Indicates whether the batch is atomic or non-atomic. If true, the batch will be executed as an atomic transaction. If false, the batch will be executed as a non-atomic pipeline.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
// Example of Atomic Batch (Transaction) in a Cluster
const transaction = new ClusterBatch(true) // Atomic (Transactional)
    .set("key", "value")
    .get("key");
const result = await client.exec(transaction, true);
console.log(result); // ["OK", "value"]

// Example of Non-Atomic Batch (Pipeline) in a Cluster
const pipeline = new ClusterBatch(false) // Non-Atomic (Pipeline)
    .set("key1", "value1")
    .set("key2", "value2")
    .get("key1")
    .get("key2");
const result = await client.exec(pipeline, true);
console.log(result); // ["OK", "OK", "value1", "value2"]

Determines whether the batch is atomic or non-atomic. If true, the batch will be executed as an atomic transaction. If false, the batch will be executed as a non-atomic pipeline.

docs.title: bitcount()
docs.text:
bitcount(key, options?): ClusterBatch

Counts the number of set bits (population counting) in the string stored at key. The options argument can optionally be provided to count the number of bits in a specific string interval.

docs.title: key
docs.text:
GlideString

The key for the string to count the set bits of.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
BitOffsetOptions

The offset options - see BitOffsetOptions.

Command Response - If options is provided, returns the number of set bits in the string interval specified by options. If options is not provided, returns the number of set bits in the string stored at key. Otherwise, if key is missing, returns 0 as it is treated as an empty string.

docs.title: bitfield()
docs.text:
bitfield(key, subcommands): ClusterBatch

Reads or modifies the array of bits representing the string that is held at key based on the specified subcommands.

docs.title: subcommands
docs.text:
BitFieldSubCommands[]

The subcommands to be performed on the binary value of the string at key, which could be any of the following:

  • BitFieldGet
  • BitFieldSet
  • BitFieldIncrBy
  • BitFieldOverflow

Command Response - An array of results from the executed subcommands:

  • BitFieldGet returns the value in BitOffset or BitOffsetMultiplier.
  • BitFieldSet returns the old value in BitOffset or BitOffsetMultiplier.
  • BitFieldIncrBy returns the new value in BitOffset or BitOffsetMultiplier.
  • BitFieldOverflow determines the behavior of the BitFieldSet and BitFieldIncrBy subcommands when an overflow or underflow occurs. BitFieldOverflow does not return a value and does not contribute a value to the array response.

docs.title: bitpos()

bitpos(key, bit, options?): ClusterBatch

Returns the position of the first bit matching the given bit value. The optional starting offset start is a zero-based index, with 0 being the first byte of the list, 1 being the next byte and so on. The offset can also be a negative number indicating an offset starting at the end of the list, with -1 being the last byte of the list, -2 being the penultimate, and so on.

docs.title: blmove()
docs.text:
blmove(source, destination, whereFrom, whereTo, timeout): ClusterBatch

Blocks the connection until it pops atomically and removes the left/right-most element to the list stored at source depending on whereFrom, and pushes the element at the first/last element of the list stored at destination depending on whereTo. BLMOVE is the blocking variant of lmove.

docs.title: bzmpop()
docs.text:
bzmpop(keys, modifier, timeout, count?): ClusterBatch

Pops a member-score pair from the first non-empty sorted set, with the given keys being checked in the order they are provided. Blocks the connection when there are no members to pop from any of the given sorted sets. BZMPOP is the blocking variant of zmpop.

docs.title: modifier
docs.text:
ScoreFilter

The element pop criteria - either ScoreFilter.MIN or ScoreFilter.MAX to pop the member with the lowest/highest score accordingly.

docs.title: timeout
docs.text:

docs.title: count?
docs.text:

Command Response - A two-element array containing the key name of the set from which the element was popped, and a GlideRecord<number> of the popped elements - see GlideRecord. If no member could be popped, returns null.

docs.title: Remarks
docs.text: BZMPOP is a client blocking command, see Valkey Glide Wiki for more details and best practices.

number

docs.title: expire()
docs.text:
expire(key, seconds, options?): ClusterBatch

Sets a timeout on key in seconds. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. If seconds is non-positive number, the key will be deleted rather than expired. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.text:

The key to set timeout on it.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:

docs.title: expireAt()
docs.text:
expireAt(key, unixSeconds, options?): ClusterBatch

Sets a timeout on key. It takes an absolute Unix timestamp (seconds since January 1, 1970) instead of specifying the number of seconds. A timestamp in the past will delete the key immediately. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted. If key already has an existing expire set, the time to live is updated to the new value. The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of key.

docs.title: key

docs.title: options?

Command Response - true if the timeout was set. false if the timeout was not set. e.g. key doesn't exist, or operation skipped due to the provided arguments.

docs.text:

docs.title: hgetex()
docs.text:

Gets hash fields and optionally sets their expiration.

docs.title: fields
docs.text:

The fields in the hash stored at key to retrieve from the database.

docs.title: options?
docs.text:
HGetExOptions

Optional arguments for the HGETEX command. See HGetExOptions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
// Get fields without setting expiration
batch.hgetex("myHash", ["field1", "field2"]);

// Get fields and set 30 second expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 30 } }
);

// Get fields and remove expiration (make persistent)
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field1", "field2"],
    { expiry: "PERSIST" }
);

// Get fields and set millisecond precision expiration
batch.hgetex(
    "myHash",
    ["field3"],
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Milliseconds, count: 5000 } }
);

Command Response - An array of values associated with the given fields, in the same order as they are requested. For every field that does not exist in the hash, a null value is returned. If key does not exist, returns an array of null values.

docs.text:
// Set fields with 60 second expiration, only if none exist
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field1: "value1", field2: "value2" },
    {
        fieldConditionalChange: HashFieldConditionalChange.ONLY_IF_NONE_EXIST,
        expiry: { type: TimeUnit.Seconds, count: 60 }

);

// Set fields and keep existing TTL
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field3: "value3" },
    { expiry: "KEEPTTL" }
);

// Set fields with Unix timestamp expiration
batch.hsetex(
    "myHash",
    { field4: "value4" },
    { expiry: { type: TimeUnit.UnixSeconds, count: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600 } }
);
